subject: I didn't outline the last letter
title: I didn't outline the last letter
preheader: I filed research on how videos hold attention, then forgot it. It shaped the last letter anyway.

lines: I pasted in research about how video creators hold attention, then forgot about it. Sitting down to draft the last letter, it came back as the outline.
A filed note sits still. This one did work.

blocks.text: The letter you got last time, about Dom at the climbing gym and the name I couldn't come up with. I didn't outline that one.

Before I wrote it I'd pasted a pile of research into my vault. A breakdown of how video creators hold attention: open loops, stakes, the reason people stay past the first few seconds. It went in messy, got filed, and I stopped thinking about it.

blocks.alt: A filed note titled How video creators hold attention, tagged reference and marketing, with one line: open loops, stakes

blocks.text: Then I sat down to draft the letter and asked for help shaping it.
The outline that came back: open on the blank where his name should be, close it fast with the name, open the bigger question about why a notes app could do that at all, pay it off at the end.

blocks.alt: The outline that came back: open on the blank where his name should be, close it fast with the name, open the bigger question, pay it off at the end

blocks.text: That is the research note. Picked up and used on the thing I was actually working on, because it was relevant, not because I remembered owning it.
Every notes system I've had was good at the filing part. Tidy titles, the right folder, tags I never went back and searched. What I had was a well organized place for my thinking to sit.
A note that gets filed is still a note sitting there. This one did something I wouldn't have known to ask for, because I'd forgotten it was mine.

Same session. My note about Dom described him by how I'd pick him out across a room, the way you'd describe anyone you met once and wanted to recognize again. Fine in my notes. It got left out of the letter, and I hadn't asked for that.
Want to be featured? Reply and show how you use Atoms day to day. We only name people with permission.
